question: Before how many weeks of pregnancy do we consider labour to be preterm?
explanation: You've got this! Any delivery that happens before completing 37 weeks of gestation is called preterm labour. Keep it up! [learn more](GNS226_U4_T001#GNS226_U4_T001_h1)

question: What two signs tell us a mother is truly in preterm labour?

options.A: Regular contractions and progressive cervical change
options.B: Complete rupture of membranes and heavy bleeding
options.C: Severe headache and blurred vision in the third trimester
options.D: High blood pressure and sudden swelling of the feet

explanation: Spotting true labour means looking for both regular tummy tightening (contractions) and signs that the cervix is actually opening up. Great job learning the clinical markers! [learn more](GNS226_U4_T001#GNS226_U4_T001_h1)

question: What is the biggest clue in a patient's history that points to a future preterm birth?

options.A: A history of mild gestational diabetes
options.C: A history of a previous preterm birth
options.D: Maternal age under twenty years old

explanation: History is a powerful teacher! A mother who has delivered early before carries the highest risk of it happening again. You are building brilliant clinical instincts. [learn more](GNS226_U4_T001#GNS226_U4_T001_h2)

question: Why do twin pregnancies so often result in early labour?

options.A: Permanent blockage of the cervical os
options.B: Excessive stretching of the uterine muscle fibers
options.C: Early closure of the maternal heart valves
options.D: Constant reduction in maternal blood volume

explanation: Think of the womb like a balloon: carrying more than one baby stretches the muscle fibers too much, sending early signals to start contracting. Makes total sense, right? [learn more](GNS226_U4_T001#GNS226_U4_T001_h2)

question: How do infections inside the uterus trigger early labour?

options.A: By causing a sudden drop in circulating maternal red blood cells
options.B: By blocking the normal production of maternal thyroid hormones
options.C: By increasing the thickness of the amniotic fluid membranes
options.D: By releasing pro-inflammatory cytokines that stimulate prostaglandins

explanation: When an infection stirs up the immune system, it releases inflammatory chemicals that act like a wake-up call for prostaglandins, triggering contractions. You're mastering the patho! [learn more](GNS226_U4_T001#GNS226_U4_T001_h3)

question: Which hormone acts like a natural relaxant to keep the uterus calm during pregnancy?
explanation: Progesterone is the uterus's best friend—it keeps everything calm and relaxed until it's time to meet the baby. Keep up the fantastic work! [learn more](GNS226_U4_T001#GNS226_U4_T001_h3)

question: What is the main use of a fetal fibronectin test in the hospital?

options.A: To rule out delivery within the next two weeks when negative
options.B: To measure the precise level of maternal blood glucose
options.C: To confirm the exact gestational age in weeks and days
options.D: To detect active bacterial infections inside the bladder

explanation: A negative fetal fibronectin test is reassuring! It's like a reliable green light telling us delivery isn't happening in the next 14 days. Brilliant clinical knowledge! [learn more](GNS226_U4_T001#GNS226_U4_T001_h4)

question: A mum at 30 weeks has contractions, but her scan shows a healthy cervical length of 35 mm. What does this mean?

options.A: The gestational age estimation is incorrect
options.B: Delivery within the next week is very unlikely
options.C: Immediate surgical delivery is required today
options.D: The patient has advanced cervical dilation

explanation: A good, long cervical length on ultrasound is great news—it tells us preterm birth isn't lurking right around the corner. You're getting the hang of this! [learn more](GNS226_U4_T001#GNS226_U4_T001_h4)

question: Why do doctors give tocolytic drugs to a mother in preterm labour?

options.A: To delay delivery for 48 hours to give steroids time to work
options.B: To permanently stop uterine contractions for the rest of the pregnancy
options.C: To cure any underlying bacterial infection causing the labour
options.D: To lower the mother's blood pressure back to normal levels

explanation: Think of tocolytic drugs as our 'pause button'—they buy crucial hours so life-saving steroids can help the baby's lungs. You are thinking like a real nurse! [learn more](GNS226_U4_T001#GNS226_U4_T001_h5)

question: Which tocolytic drug is usually avoided past 32 weeks because it can affect the baby's heart circulation?
explanation: Indomethacin is a prostaglandin blocker, but we have to be careful using it late in pregnancy so it doesn't cause early closure of the baby's ductus arteriosus. Excellent pharmacological safety! [learn more](GNS226_U4_T001#GNS226_U4_T001_h5)

question: How do antenatal steroids help a preterm baby?

options.A: By stimulating the production of lung surfactant
options.B: By stopping all internal bleeding in the brain
options.C: By increasing the baby's birth weight instantly
options.D: By preventing any future childhood infections

explanation: Steroids give the baby's lungs a wonderful boost by helping build surfactant, keeping those tiny air sacs from collapsing after birth. Beautiful concept to remember! [learn more](GNS226_U4_T001#GNS226_U4_T001_h6)

question: For which age group of pregnancy are steroids routinely recommended if early birth threatens?
explanation: Babies born between 24 and 34 weeks benefit the absolute most from these lung-maturing steroids. You're storing up great clinical facts for your exams and wards! [learn more](GNS226_U4_T001#GNS226_U4_T001_h6)

question: Why is continuous electronic fetal monitoring so important during preterm labour?

options.A: Preterm fetuses tolerate the stress of contractions poorly
options.B: It stops the progress of cervical dilation automatically
options.C: It is the only way to calculate the exact due date
options.D: It prevents the mother from experiencing any back pain

explanation: Preterm babies have delicate reserves, so watching the monitor closely helps us catch signs of distress early. You're learning top-tier patient safety! [learn more](GNS226_U4_T001#GNS226_U4_T001_h7)

question: Who needs to be right there at the bedside when a very early preterm baby is delivered?

options.A: The hospital administrator and billing officers
options.B: An orthopedic surgeon and surgical assistants
options.C: A specialized hospital social worker and dietician
options.D: Neonatal resuscitation and paediatric team members

explanation: Teamwork is everything in the labour ward! Having the neonatal experts ready ensures the tiny newborn gets immediate respiratory help. Fantastic clinical judgment! [learn more](GNS226_U4_T001#GNS226_U4_T001_h7)

question: What is the main cause of Respiratory Distress Syndrome in a premature baby?

options.A: A weak and underdeveloped heart muscle
options.B: An infection in the urinary tract

explanation: Without enough surfactant to keep them open, the baby's tiny air sacs stick together and collapse. Knowing this helps you understand why we push for steroid coverage! [learn more](GNS226_U4_T001#GNS226_U4_T001_h8)

question: Which serious condition involves tissue damage and inflammation in the bowels of a premature baby?
explanation: Necrotizing enterocolitis (NEC) is a tough bowel complication in preemies where parts of the intestine can suffer tissue death. You're mastering complex neonatal nursing topics! [learn more](GNS226_U4_T001#GNS226_U4_T001_h8)

question: A mum on tocolytics says her chest feels tight and she's struggling to breathe. What is your immediate nursing action?

options.A: Document the findings as a normal side effect
options.B: Stop the medication infusion and notify the doctor
options.C: Encourage the patient to take deep and slow breaths
options.D: Increase the intravenous fluid rate immediately

explanation: Patient safety first! Chest tightness can point to dangerous fluid overload (pulmonary edema) from tocolytics, so your best move is stopping the infusion right away and calling the doctor. [learn more](GNS226_U4_T001#GNS226_U4_T001_h9)

question: What is one of the best ways a nurse can comfort parents facing an unexpected preterm birth?

options.A: Arranging a pre-delivery visit with the neonatal team
options.B: Telling them not to worry about the baby's outcome
options.C: Limiting all visitors to ensure complete physical rest
options.D: Delaying any discussion about the baby until after birth

explanation: Fear of the unknown is heavy. Introducing parents to the NICU team beforehand gives them comfort and a clear picture of what to expect. You have a true nurse's heart! [learn more](GNS226_U4_T001#GNS226_U4_T001_h9)
